dunjko-review-aim-physicist-reader: Section I, p.3: the authors state the review's aim and intended reader in these words.
dunjko-review-not-balanced: Section I, p.3 'Remark': the authors say the survey is not fully balanced and name Section VII as the example. Type is a limit, not a setup.
dunjko-quantum-ai-speculative: Section VII.C, p.88: the authors state that their quantum AI considerations are highly speculative and that genuine AI research has barely broken ground.
dunjko-review-scope: Abstract, p.1: 'In this review, we describe the main ideas, recent developments, and progress...'. Stored value matches the quotes.
dupont-algorithm-definition: Main text p.2: the iterative freeze-and-reduce algorithm and its steps #1 to #4 are the authors' own definition.
dupont-hardware-aspen-m3: Main text p.3 and Methods p.5: Rigetti Aspen-M-3, 79 qubits, planar square-octagon topology, as the authors state.
dupont-truncated-qaoa-setup: Main text p.3: truncated one-layer QAOA, only gates within 2 swap cycles kept, with the reason (noise) given by the authors.
dupont-benchmark-instances-and-freezing: Main text p.3: 10 random SK instances for N = 8, 24, 40, 56, 72, k = 1 variable frozen per step, two-body expectation selection.
dupont-mps-bond-dimension: Methods p.6: the authors state the MPS simulation setting, bond dimension 64 for the shallow 4-layer brick-wall circuits, used for Fig. 3.
dupont-hard-constraints-limit: Main text p.4: the authors limit their constraint-handling idea to some classes of constraints, because general satisfiability is NP-complete (textbook background).
dupont-portfolio-limits: Appendix S7 'Outlook' p.16: the authors say it would be precipitate to conclude, because the greedy baseline is strong and there is one instance per size with N <= 10.
dupont-rigor-future-work: Main text p.4 (Discussion): the authors say that proving the outperformance rigorously remains future work. Stored value matches the quote.
ion-trap-qubit-device: Section II.A p.2: 138Ba+ trapped-ion qubit, coherence time 5 ms and Rabi pi-time 12 microseconds, as the authors state.
ion-trap-six-layer-limit: Section II.A p.3: the DDS memory limit of 16 phase steps limits the layers to six, in the authors' words.
ion-trap-ansatz-definition: Section II.B p.3, Eqs. 3 and 4: Ansatz A and Ansatz B are the authors' definitions.
ion-trap-two-step-training: Section II.C p.4 and Fig. 3: the two-step protocol (simulation with chi squared, then hardware fine-tuning of Aq) is the authors' procedure. The value does not claim the improvement.
ion-trap-second-step-condition: Section II.C p.4: the authors state the second step works only if the loss near the minimum is shallow.
ion-trap-z-gate-by-phase: Section II.D p.5: the authors choose to perform Rz by laser phase change. The error remark follows from that design as they state it.
ion-trap-depth-halving: Section II.D p.5, Eqs. 9 to 12 and Fig. 4(a): the authors define the R(gamma, delta) compression and its pairwise-only limit.
ion-trap-fidelity-by-comparison: Section II.D p.5, Eqs. 13 and 14: the authors measure fidelity by direct comparison with a label state, not tomography.
ion-trap-circle-problem-definition: Section III p.6: the circle problem, balanced classes and 50% random baseline, as the authors define it.
ion-trap-asim-error-meaning: Section III p.6 and Table I caption p.9: the error in Asim is the standard deviation of 10 repeated trials on the same dataset.
ion-trap-classical-benchmark-setup: Section III p.7 and Table I caption p.9: single-hidden-layer NN and SVM benchmarks, NN with an equivalent number of parameters.
ion-trap-hypersphere-scope-limit: Appendix B p.12: for 4 or more dimensions the half-volume n-ball does not fit in the hypercube; the authors say the effect on the random classifier is not taken into account.
ion-trap-limited-optimization: Table I caption p.9: 'Only two cases have been further optimized using an exploration done only with the quantum device.' Stored value matches the quote.
ion-trap-setup: Section III p.6: 200 training points, 1000 test points, and the experimental step carried out in only two cases. The new value fixes the stored value's loose 'two steps' wording and matches the passage.
bosonic-perspective-scope: Abstract p.2 and Section 1 p.3: the authors state what the perspective reviews and that it focuses on cQED qumodes.
bosonic-qumode-definition: Section 1 p.3: the qumode is introduced as 'known as a qumode', with its infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. Standard background, defined in the paper.

theory_low.dunjko-rps-same-learning-efficiency: Section VII.A, p.82: one sentence resting on 'by definition' behavioural equivalence of the rPS and quantum rPS agents. The equivalence is taken from the cited PS work and not proved here. The sample-complexity remark is the authors' interpretation.
theory_low.dupont-greedy-guarantee: Main text p.2: 'The essential point is...' is an informal argument, not a theorem with a proof. The guarantee holds 'under reasonable assumption' and is tied to the Methods baseline, which is an averaging argument.
theory_low.dupont-optimal-strings-preserved: Main text p.2: a one-sentence claim with no proof, not stated as a theorem.
theory_low.dupont-greedy-baseline-value: Fig. 2 caption p.3, main text p.4, Methods pp.6-7: 0.848497 comes from an averaging argument (random-walk mean, Maclaurin sum, Parisi constant from refs [31,32], finite-size constant from [30]). It is not stated or proved as a theorem. The comparison to the noisy QAOA is a measured result.
theory_low.dupont-random-sampling-equivalence: Appendix S2 p.11: a statistical estimate from a Gaussian approximation and the Gumbel limit (Eq. S4), valid only away from the tail. An estimate, not a proved result.
theory_low.dupont-ring-graph-greedy-ratio: Appendix S8 p.17: an analytic average (Eqs. S6 to S11) from an expected-value argument over random freezing, not stated as a theorem or lemma. 5/6 = 0.833333 is the derived mean.
